findings.title: Occurrence context drops the prepared schedule_type display
findings.body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it on that copy with monitor.get_schedule_type_display() so the issue occurrence can carry a human-readable schedule. The returned context ignores that copy and sends monitor_environment.monitor.config instead. The display conversion is discarded, so every monitor incident occurrence published to Kafka still has the raw schedule_type. The returned config is also the live in-memory model dict, so any later mutation of the occurrence context config mutates the monitor instance.

findings.title: failure_issue_threshold does not require N consecutive failures
findings.body: try_incident_threshold is what opens a monitor incident after failure_issue_threshold consecutive failures. The threshold==1 path correctly uses only the current failed check-in. For any larger threshold it loads at most that many latest check-ins of any status and returns without opening an incident only if one of them is CheckInStatus.OK. It never requires the window to contain failure_issue_threshold rows, and it never requires those rows to be ERROR, MISSED, or TIMEOUT. A monitor set to threshold 3 whose first check-in fails therefore has a one-row window with no OK, and this still sets the environment to MonitorStatus.ERROR, get_or_creates a MonitorIncident, emits issue occurrences, and sends monitor_environment_failed. An in-progress check-in in the window counts as one of the N slots the same way, so a single real failure can both pass this gate and be published as a failure occurrence. Users who raised the threshold above 1 still get incidents and issues immediately.
